 The governors are asking for an additional $3 billion in funding.
 This file photo shows a Maine home being refueled with heating oil. Advertisement Updated: 8:07 PM EST Nov 9, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Richard Maj Producer Gov. Janet Mills joins New England governors to call for increased LIHEAP funding
 The governors are asking for an additional $3 billion in funding.
 Updated: 8:07 PM EST Nov 9, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Richard Maj Producer AUGUSTA, Maine — Gov. Janet Mills joined governors of New England states to call on Congress to increase funding for the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP).
 In a letter to congressional appropriations leadership , the governors of all six states in New England call for an additional $3 billion, which would bring the total program funding for LIHEAP up to $7 billion. The governors say the additional funding would help vulnerable households manage rising energy costs. 
 Advertisement "LIHEAP provides essential assistance to these households in every region of the country, helping families manage both winter heating and summer cooling costs. While energy needs vary by geography and season, the challenge is the same: ensuring that vulnerable Americans can afford the energy necessary to remain safe in their homes," the governors wrote. "These pressures are particularly acute in New England, where cold winters, older housing, and a heavy reliance on delivered heating fuel leave families especially exposed to the dramatic price increases America is currently experiencing."
 “No one should be cold in their homes because Trump decided to wage an unnecessary, unwanted war with Iran,” Gov. Mills said in a statement. “That’s why I’m joining my fellow New England governors to call on Congress to release billions in federal funding for LIHEAP to provide immediate relief for vulnerable families as winter approaches.”
 This comes after last month, heating oil prices in Maine reached a record $6.04 per gallon, according to the Maine Department of Energy Resources.
